4952.t: From Phoenician (compare Hebrew נֵרְדְּ (nērd), Aramaic נִרְדָּא (nirdā), Akkadian 𒆠𒆗 (HIRIM /⁠lardu⁠/), Arabic رَنْد (rand), Old South Arabian 𐩧𐩬𐩵 (rnd)), possibly from Sanskrit नलद (nálada, “Indian narde”) (although a Semitic-to-Indian loan has also been…

4954.t: Derived from νομίζω (nomízō, “to use customarily”) + -μα (-ma, “nominal suffix”).

4947.t: From νέμω (némō, “to pasture; to graze”) + -ός (-ós, deverbal nominal suffix). Compare ἀγρός (agrós).

4944.t: Sometimes derived from a Proto-Indo-European *me(-)mbʰ-e-, and compared with obsolete English mump (“to cheat, swindle”), Gothic 𐌱𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌼𐍀𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bimampjan, “to mock”).

4992.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *per- Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-ih₂ Proto-Indo-European *périh₂ Proto-Hellenic *péřřa Ancient Greek πεῖρα (peîră) Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂…

4918.t: From Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d-. Cognates include Sanskrit मद॑ति (mádati), म॒मत्ति॑ (mamátti), Latin madeō, and Old Irish maidid.

4931.t: From μετα- (meta-, indicating change) + φέρω (phérō, “bear, carry”).

4902.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀖𐀜 (ku-mi-no), borrowed from Semitic, compare Ge'ez ከሚን (kämin), ካሚን (kamin), ከሙን (kämun), ከሜን (kämen), Arabic كَمُّون (kammūn), Hebrew כַּמֹּון (kammōn), Aramaic כַּמֹּונָֹא / ܩܰܡܽܘܢܳܐ (kammōnā, “cumin”), ultimately from…

4920.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *məlakos, from Proto-Indo-European *ml̥h₂ekos, from *melh₂- (“soft, weak”), which Beekes separates from the "grind, rub" sense, though this is disputed.

4911.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *lewotrón, whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀩𐀺𐀵𐀫 (re-wo-to-ro /⁠lewotrón⁠/), from Proto-Indo-European *léwh₃trom (“that which is used for washing”), from *lewh₃- (“to wash, bathe”); see there for further cognates.

4915.t: Traditionally viewed as a suffix -ρ- (-r-), added to a u-stem from the root of Sanskrit लभते (labhate, “to take, seize”). Beekes considers the suffix -υρ- (-ūr-) to be Pre-Greek.

4955.t: Of unclear origin. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *new- (“to make a push, nod”).

4950.t: From νωθής (nōthḗs, “sluggish, slothful”) + -ρός (-rós, adjective suffix). The origin of νωθής (nōthḗs, “slow, indolent, stubborn”) is disputed.

4941.t: Unclear. The word has been linked with μυών (muṓn, “cluster of muscles”) because both marrow and muscles are soft in texture.

4900.t: Compared by Beekes to γυργαθός (gurgathós, “wicker basket”), κύαθος (kúathos, “wine ladle”), and ὁρμαθός (hormathós, “cluster chain”) and declared Pre-Greek, likely based on semantic domain and suffix.

4906.t: Ending like ἀπήνη (apḗnē) and καπάνα (kapā́na). According to Beekes, the word is evidently Pre-Greek, because of the prenasalization and the suffix -ήνη.

4904.t: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *lengʰ- (“to obtain”), although—according to Beekes—no cognates are known.

4934.t: From μετα- (metă-, “behind”) + φρήν (phrḗn, “midriff”), literally “the part behind the midriff”.

4962.t: οἶκος (oîkos, “home”) + -ίζω (-ízō, “a suffix forming a verb from a noun”)

4979.t: From παραλογίζομαι (părălogĭ́zomai, “to cheat; to use fallacies”) + -μός (-mós).

4959.t: From οἰκέω (oikéō, “inhabit, dwell”) + -τός (-tós, “A suffix creating verbal adjectives of possibility, either active or passive”)
